comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting measurement and fee recognition for loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans are reported at outstanding principal net of unearned income, charge-offs, and deferred fees, with origination fees and direct costs deferred and recognized over the loan life using a constant effective yield methodology.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC disclose that loans (excluding those with the fair value option elected) are presented net of unamortized discounts/premiums, deferred loan fees, and costs. JPM explicitly states these amounts were not material as of Dec 31, 2024 and 2023, while BAC describes the mechanical application (net of unearned income, charge-offs, deferred fees/costs) and the amortization methodology (constant effective yield) without explicitly quantifying materiality in this specific sentence, though the topic of presentation is identical.

sentences.text: (b)Loans (other than those for which the fair value option has been elected) are presented net of unamortized discounts and premiums and net deferred loan fees or costs.
These amounts were not material as of December 31, 2024 and 2023.

Loans, with the exception of loans accounted for under the fair value option, are reported at their outstanding principal balances net of any unearned income, charge-offs, unamortized deferred fees and costs on originated loans, and for purchased loans, net of any unamortized premiums or discounts.
Unearned income, discounts and premiums are amortized to interest income using a constant effective yield methodology.

comparisons.peer_topic: Classification and reporting of held-for-investment loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans held-for-investment are reported at outstanding principal balances net of unearned income and unamortized deferred fees, with specific treatments for credit card receivables and loans under the fair value option. Loan origination fees and direct origination costs are deferred and recognized over the life of the related loans.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Citi disclose that held-for-investment loans are reported at outstanding principal balances net of unearned income and unamortized deferred fees and costs. Citi explicitly excludes credit card receivables and loans under the fair value option from this specific net presentation rule, whereas JPM excludes only loans under the fair value option. Both mention the deferral and recognition of fees over the loan life.

sentences.text: (b)Loans (other than those for which the fair value option has been elected) are presented net of unamortized discounts and premiums and net deferred loan fees or costs.
For the discount associated with First Republic loans, refer to Note 34 on pages 319-321.

Loans that are held-for-investment (HFI) are classified as Loans on the Consolidated Balance Sheet and are reported at their outstanding principal balances net of any unearned income and unamortized deferred fees and costs, except for credit card receivable balances, which include accrued interest and fees, and certain loans for which Citi has elected the fair value option (see "Loans at Fair Value" below).
Loan origination fees and certain direct origination costs are generally deferred and recognized as adjustments to income over the lives of the related loans.

comparisons.peer_summary: Loans held for investment at amortized cost include net deferred fees and unamortized premiums/discounts, which were less than 1% of such loans in December 2024 and 2023. Substantially all loans had floating interest rates in both periods.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and GS disclose that loans held for investment at amortized cost include net deferred fees and unamortized premiums/discounts. GS provides a quantitative measure, stating these amounts were less than 1% of such loans as of Dec 2024 and 2023. JPM states these amounts were not material as of the same dates. Both confirm the inclusion of these items in the amortized cost basis.

sentences.text: (b)Loans (other than those for which the fair value option has been elected) are presented net of unamortized discounts and premiums and net deferred loan fees or costs.
These amounts were not material as of December 31, 2024 and 2023.

• Loans held for investment that are accounted for at amortized cost include net deferred fees and costs, and unamortized premiums and discounts, which are amortized over the life of the loan. These amounts were less than 1% of loans accounted for at amortized cost as of both December 2024 and December 2023.

comparisons.peer_summary: Interest income on performing loans is accrued at the contractual rate, while purchase price discounts/premiums and net deferred fees/costs are amortized over the loan life to produce a level rate of return.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and MS disclose the treatment of purchase price discounts/premiums and net deferred loan fees/costs in the context of loan accounting. JPM states these are presented net (and are not material) for loans excluding the fair value option. MS specifies that these items are amortized into interest income over the life of the loan to produce a level rate of return. Both address the same components (discounts/premiums, fees/costs) and their impact on the loan's carrying value/income recognition.

sentences.text: (b)Loans (other than those for which the fair value option has been elected) are presented net of unamortized discounts and premiums and net deferred loan fees or costs.
For the discount associated with First Republic loans, refer to Note 34 on pages 319-321.
Purchase price discounts or premiums, as well as net deferred loan fees or costs, are amortized into interest income over the life of the loan to produce a level rate of return.
